page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-64 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of stress-ng tests. Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics, also rank in the top 25%. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth are in the top 25%, large-block uncached read bandwidth falls into the middle 50%. Database operations and ray tracing benchmarks demonstrate strong performance, whereas Redis SET operations, static web serving, and software compilation align with average tier results.

Given its high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU and dedicated AMD EPYC cores, this server type provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The absence of bundled local storage means storage-heavy operations must rely on network-attached options. The server is suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data processing, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
